title: Approximating velocity fields with planted attractors via Neural-ODEs for classification purposes
authors: Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico, Duccio Fanelli, Lorenzo Buffoni, Lorenzo Chicchi, Diego Febbe, Raffaele Marino
abstract: In this work, Neural ODEs equipped with a curated collection of equilibrium points have been successfully employed for classification tasks.The planted attractors serve as indicators for the target classes, while the velocity field leveraging the universal approximation capabilities of the architecture shapes the dynamical landscape.This process defines the basins of attraction of the trained model, effectively directing each input provided as an initial condition toward its corresponding destination target.
summary: This paper proposes ConsNODEs, a novel classification method that embeds target classes as stable attractors within a Neural ODE framework. By constraining the network's velocity field to guide inputs toward these fixed points, it creates an interpretable dynamical classifier. The work validates this approach on standard datasets and theoretically shows its consistency by deriving it from a coupled system in the limit of weak coupling.
main_problem: The work develops a novel classification framework by integrating planted attractors into Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural-ODEs) to create an interpretable dynamical system for pattern recognition.
main_result: The proposed ConsNODEs successfully route initial conditions toward distinct, stable planted equilibria corresponding to target classes, showing competitive performance against static MLPs on benchmarks like Fashion-MNIST.
method: Classification is achieved by training the ODE parameters such that the learned velocity field forces trajectories towards predefined fixed points (attractors) representing class prototypes. The method uses terminal-time regression loss and QR decomposition for parameter enforcement.
model_or_system: The core model is a Neural ODE, $\dot{x}(t) = F_	heta(x(t))$, whose parameters are constrained to ensure the existence of fixed points at specified attractors $\{ ar{x}^{(\ell)}\}$. The framework also analyzes this structure by deriving it from an augmented coupled system in the singular limit ($\varepsilon 	o 0$).
key_observables: Test Accuracy, FLOPs, Inference Time, and the distance/deviation metrics ($e_x(t), e_M(t)$) used to confirm convergence to the slow manifold.
important_parameters: The small coupling parameter $\varepsilon$, the number of classes $C$, and the integration time horizon $T$.
main_assumptions: The planted features defining the attractors are assumed to be linearly independent ($	ext{rank}(S) = C$ with $m > C$). The method assumes that the constrained network class retains universal approximation capabilities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate trajectory routing in toy examples, show convergence diagnostics ($e_x(t), e_M(t)$) approaching zero as $\varepsilon 	o 0$, and compare accuracy vs. integration time to find an optimal inference horizon $t_{	ext{best}}$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the constrained Neural-ODE framework using planted attractors for classification, demonstrating its structure via linear algebra constraints. It then validates this approach on benchmarks (Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10) by comparing it to static MLPs. Finally, it theoretically grounds the model by showing that a complex coupled system reduces to this modified Neural-ODE in the singular limit $\varepsilon 	o 0$.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between dynamical systems theory (slow manifold reduction) and machine learning architectures provides a physically motivated interpretation of deep learning models, which is highly relevant for modeling open quantum systems dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Two-spirals dynamical classification with planted equilibria (ConsNODEs). (Left) Training set (two interleaving spirals) with planted equilibria marked by red crosses. (Center) Learned vector field visualized via streamlines, showing how trajectories are routed toward the corresponding class equilibrium. (Right) Induced partition of the plane obtained by integrating each initial condition to time T and applying the nearest-equilibrium decoder (21).

FIG. 2: Accuracy of ConsNODEs on Fashion-MNIST as a function of the integration time. The validation and test accuracy rapidly approach a plateau before the full training horizon T, showing that in practice the classifier can be evaluated with a shorter inference horizon tbest, while essentially preserving the same accuracy.
FIG. 3: CIFAR-10 accuracy learning curves (mean ± standard deviation over 5 runs) comparing the parameter-matched MLP head and the QR-planted dynamical head (ConsNODEs).

FIG. 4: Projected trajectories of the coupled model (22) in the x-space for four values of ε (same trained matrices (A1, A2, b1, b2) as ConsNODEs). As ε decreases, the trajectories rapidly align with those induced by the reduced dynamics (24), reflecting attraction to the slow manifold M in (25).

FIG. 5: Diagnostics for the coupled system (22) at small ε. (Left) Mean deviation between the projected coupled trajectory xε(t) and the reduced trajectory x(t) of (24). (Right) Mean distance to the slow manifold M defined by u = A2x + b2. Both plots support the interpretation of model (24) as the ε →0 reduction of the two populations model.
